column1: Drought, housing expansion, and oversupply of tinder make for bigger, hotter fires in the western United States
column2: 干旱、住房扩张和可燃物过剩导致美国西部火灾更大更猛烈。

column1: Wildfires are becoming an increasing menace in the western United States, with Southern California being the hardest hit area.
column2: 野火正日益成为美国西部日益严重的威胁，其中南加州受灾最严重。

column1: There’s a reason fire squads battling more frequent blazes in Southern California are having such difficulty containing the flames, despite better preparedness than ever and decades of experience fighting fires fanned by the ‘Santa Ana Winds’.
column2: 南加州的消防队面对越来越频繁的大火，如此难以控制火势是有原因的，尽管他们准备得比以往任何时候都充分，也有数十年扑救圣安娜风助长的大火的经验。
column7: having such difficulty|做某事如此困难

column1: The wildfires themselves, experts say, are generally hotter, faster, and spread more erratically than in the past.
column2: 专家指出，这些野火通常比过去更加剧烈、蔓延速度更快，且扩散方式也更为混乱。

column1: Megafires, also called ‘siege fires’, are the increasingly frequent blazes that burn 500,000 acres or more - 10 times the size of the average forest fire of 20 years ago.
column2: 特大野火也叫“围困式大火”。这种火灾越来越频繁，每场烧过的面积达50万英亩或更多，是20年前一场森林火灾平均过火面积的十倍。

column1: Some recent wildfires are among the biggest ever in California in terms of acreage burned, according to state figures and news reports.
column2: 据官方数据和新闻报道，就燃烧面积而言，一些最近的火灾是加州有史以来最大的。

column1: One explanation for the trend to more superhot fires is that the region, which usually has dry summers, has had significantly below normal precipitation in many recent years.
column2: 这种超级高温火灾现象增多的一个原因可能是，该地区的夏季通常比较干燥，但近年来降水量明显低于正常水平。

column1: Another reason, experts say, is related to the century-long policy of the US Forest Service to stop wildfires as quickly as possible.
column2: 专家们还指出，另一个原因是美国林务局长达一个世纪之久的政策，即致力于尽快扑灭野火。

column1: The unintentional consequence has been to halt the natural eradication of underbrush, now the primary fuel for megafires.
column2: 这种无意的后果就是阻碍了灌木丛的自然消退过程，而灌木丛原本是大型火灾的主要燃料来源。

column1: Three other factors contribute to the trend, they add.
column2: 另外三个因素也推动了这一趋势，他们补充道。

column1: First is climate change, marked by a 1-degree Fahrenheit rise in average yearly temperature across the western states.
column2: 首先是气候变化，西部各州年均气温已上升1华氏度。

column1: Second is fire seasons that on average are 78 days longer than they were 20 years ago.
column2: 其次，火灾季节平均比20年前长了78天。

column1: Third is increased construction of homes in wooded areas.
column2: 第三是森林地区住宅建设的扩张。

column1: ‘We are increasingly building our homes in fire-prone ecosystems,’ says Dominik Kulakowski, adjunct professor of biology at Clark University Graduate School of Geography in Worcester, Massachusetts.
column2: “我们越来越常在火灾易发的生态系统中建房，”多米尼克·库拉科夫斯基说。他是马萨诸塞州伍斯特市克拉克大学地理研究生院的生物学兼职教授。

column1: ‘Doing that in many of the forests of the western US is like building homes on the side of an active volcano.’
column2: 在美国西部许多森林里进行这样的建设，就像在活火山的山坡上建造房屋一样危险。

column1: In California, where population growth has averaged more than 600,000 a year for at least a decade, more residential housing is being built.
column2: 在加利福尼亚州，过去至少十年里，人口年均增长超过60万，住宅建设正在加快。

column1: ‘What once was open space is now residential homes providing fuel to make fires burn with greater intensity,’ says Terry McHale of the California Department of Forestry firefighters’ union.
column2: ‘曾经是空地的地方，如今已变为住宅区，这些住宅为火灾提供了燃料，使火势燃烧得更加猛烈’，加州林业消防队联盟的特里·麦克黑尔说。

column1: ‘With so much dryness, so many communities to catch fire, so many fronts to fight, it becomes an almost incredible job.’
column2: ‘在如此干燥的条件下，面对如此众多的社区起火和如此多的前线需要扑灭，这几乎成了难以置信的工作。’

column1: That said, many experts give California high marks for making progress on preparedness in recent years, after some of the largest fires in state history scorched thousands of acres, burned thousands of homes, and killed numerous people.
column2: 话虽如此，许多专家仍对加州近年来在防火准备方面取得的进展给予高度评价。在此之前，加州经历了该州有史以来规模最大的几场火灾，数千英亩土地被烧焦，数千栋住宅被烧毁，还有许多人丧生。
column5: give California high marks|给予加州高度评价
column9: some of the largest|规模最大的几场

column1: Stung in the past by criticism of bungling that allowed fires to spread when they might have been contained, personnel are meeting the peculiar challenges of neighborhood—and canyon—hopping fires better than previously, observers say.
column2: 消防人员过去曾因处置失当，让本有可能得到控制的火势蔓延而饱受批评。据观察人士说，如今他们应对火势跨越社区和峡谷蔓延所带来的特殊挑战，比过去做得更好。
column8: might have been contained|本有可能得到控制

column1: State promises to provide more up-to-date engines, planes, and helicopters to fight fires have been fulfilled.
column2: 州政府承诺提供更先进的消防车、飞机和直升机用于灭火的承诺已得到落实。

column1: Firefighters’ unions that in the past complained of dilapidated equipment, old fire engines, and insufficient blueprints for fire safety are now praising the state’s commitment, noting that funding for firefighting has increased, despite huge cuts in many other programs.
column2: 消防员工会过去曾抱怨装备破旧、消防车老化，消防安全规划也不够完善，如今却称赞州政府对消防工作的重视。他们指出，尽管许多其他项目的经费大幅削减，消防经费却增加了。

column1: ‘We are pleased that the current state administration has been very proactive in its support of us, and [has] come through with budgetary support of the infrastructure needs we have long sought,’ says Mr. McHale of the firefighters’ union.
column2: ‘我们很高兴，现任政府在支持我们方面表现得非常积极，并已提供我们长期所寻求的基础设施预算支持，’消防员工会的麦克黑尔先生表示。

column1: Besides providing money to upgrade the fire engines that must traverse the mammoth state and wind along serpentine canyon roads, the state has invested in better command-and-control facilities as well as in the strategies to run them.
column2: 除了拨款升级消防车——这些车辆必须穿越幅员辽阔的加州，沿蜿蜒的峡谷道路行驶——州政府还投资改善指挥与控制设施，并为这些设施的运行方案投入了资金。

column1: ‘In the fire sieges of earlier years, we found that other jurisdictions and states were willing to offer mutual-aid help, but we were not able to communicate adequately with them,’ says Kim Zagaris, chief of the state’s Office of Emergency Services Fire and Rescue Branch.
column2: “在早些年的大火灾中，我们发现其他辖区和州愿意提供互助援助，但我们无法与他们充分沟通，”火灾应急服务部门消防救援处负责人金·扎加里斯说。

column1: After a commission examined and revamped communications procedures, the statewide response ‘has become far more professional and responsive,’ he says.
column2: 在委员会对通信流程进行审查与改进后，全州的应对机制‘变得更加专业且反应迅速’，他说。

column1: There is a sense among both government officials and residents that the speed, dedication, and coordination of firefighters from several states and jurisdictions are resulting in greater efficiency than in past ‘siege fire’ situations.
column2: 政府官员和居民都有这样一种感受：来自多个州和辖区的消防员行动迅速、尽职尽责、配合默契，因此比过去应对“围困式大火”时更有效率。

column1: In recent years, the Southern California region has improved building codes, evacuation procedures, and procurement of new technology.
column2: 近年来，南加州改进了建筑规范、疏散程序和新技术的采购方式。

column1: ‘I am extraordinarily impressed by the improvements we have witnessed,’ says Randy Jacobs, a Southern California-based lawyer who has had to evacuate both his home and business to escape wildfires.
column2: “我们亲眼看到的这些改进，给我留下了极其深刻的印象。”在南加州执业的律师兰迪·雅各布斯说。为了躲避野火，他曾不得不从住所和工作场所撤离。

column1: ‘Notwithstanding all the damage that will continue to be caused by wildfires, we will no longer suffer the loss of life endured in the past because of the fire prevention and firefighting measures that have been put in place,’ he says.
column2: “尽管野火仍将造成种种损失，我们再也不会像过去那样有人丧生了，因为各项防火和灭火措施已经落实。”他说。
